newsitem.title: GERMANY: Independent Research sees DAX at 3,350 in H1 1997.
newsitem.headline: Independent Research sees DAX at 3,350 in H1 1997.

text.p: Germany's blue chip DAX index is likely to surge some 14 percent to hit a record high of 3,350 points by May or June this year, the Frankfurt-based brokerage firm Independent Research predicted on Tuesday.
In its market forecast for 1997, the firm said the dollar would hit a high of 1.65 against the mark in the second quarter of 1997 while bond yields would reach a low of 4.9 percent.
"The German market will be very interesting in the first half of the year," said Pierre Drach, managing director of the brokerage, which was established in 1995.
Drach said expectations for strong economic growth in Germany this year would likely not be fulfilled, so that investors would not have to worry about interest rate rises to curb inflation.
The weighted DAX price-earnings ratio would be a healthy 17.63 percent in 1997 and 15.53 percent in 1998.
However Independent Research is expecting a weaker second half to the year, with the DAX seen ending 1997 at just 3,050, the dollar at 1.60 marks and yields back up to 5.20 percent.
"Investors should get out at the right moment. That could be as soon as May," said Drach.
Independent Research named as its stocks of the year chemical firm BASF AG, Deutsche Bank AG, Deutsche Lufthansa AG, MAN AG and Volkswagen.
Likely underperformers were drugs manufacturer Schering AG and Preussag AG, the engineering firm.
The company has also slapped an "underweight" tag on BMW, Bayerische Vereinsbank AG, retailer Karstadt AG and steel group Thyssen AG.
